To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ultrasound technology can be effectively used in the synthesis of cetyl ester.
the application of ultrasound irradiation to enzymatic synthesis has the potential to reduce the reaction time by 50% as well as to improve the yield by 20%.
ultrasound supported synthesis of cetyl ester using CALB™1000 lipase is a promising alternative to conventional mechanical stirring method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
optimisation and kinetic studies of enzymatic synthesis of cetyl esters under ultrasound irradiation.
the application of ultrasound irradiation for the optimisation and kinetic modelling of enzymatic synthesis of cetyl ester.
the optimisation of process parameters and kinetic studies for enzymatic synthesis of cetyl ester using lipase under ultrasound irradiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the application of ultrasound to enzymatic synthesis can reduce reaction time, enhance product yield, improve reaction rate and reduce the amount of enzyme required for the synthesis.
ultrasound technology has a great potential to improve the efficiency and productivity of enzymatic esterification reactions.
the ultrasound supported enzymatic synthesis of cetyl ester was faster, more efficient and eco-friendly than the conventional mechanical stirring method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application of ultrasound irradiation to the synthesis of cetyl ester is a promising alternative to conventional methods.
ultrasound technology is an efficient tool for enzymatic synthesis of cetyl ester.
ultrasound supported synthesis is a promising alternative for the production of cetyl oleates and other long chain esters with high conversion and purity in short duration of time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ultrasound technology is a viable alternative to mechanical agitation in enzymatic esterification reactions.
ultrasound can be used as a green technology for synthesis of cosmetic emollients like cetyl oleate.
ultrasound irradiation can accelerate enzymatic reactions and reduce the time required to achieve equilibrium.
